- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias, especially if recent prices are falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent volatility, true outcome often reverses or drops; introduce mean reversion logic or reduce slope after 3+ consecutive rising forecasts.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0) and history shows low volatility, model tends to lag; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for delayed reaction.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after model’s peak, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5–7 days to avoid overconfidence in upward momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use sentiment + recent 7-day mean to adjust forecast midpoint if sentiment shifts sharply.
